content.title: About
content.content: Pine nuts are the edible seeds of pine cones (Pinus spp.). They are small, light‑green to creamy in color, with a delicate buttery‑nutty flavor and a crisp texture. They are eaten raw, lightly toasted, or used in sauces, pastes, and baked goods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pine nuts are harvested from the cones of pine trees, not from true nuts.
One pine nut weighs about 0.5–1 g; a kilogram contains roughly 2 000–3 000 nuts.
They have been a staple in Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, and Asian cuisines for centuries.
Some pine species can live for over 1 000 years, providing a long‑term source of nuts.
Pine nuts are a key ingredient in pesto, salads, rice and pasta dishes.

items.title: Rich in monounsaturated fats
items.content: The majority of the fat in pine nuts is monounsaturated, which supports heart health.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative damage.

items.title: Contains magnesium and zinc
items.content: These minerals are important for muscle function, nervous system health, and immunity.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Pine nuts provide calcium, phosphorus, and vitamin K, which contribute to bone mineralization.

items.title: Provides protein and fiber
items.content: A modest amount of plant protein and dietary fiber helps promote satiety.

items.title: Tree‑nut allergy
items.content: People allergic to tree nuts may react to pine nuts, potentially experiencing severe reactions.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Pine nuts are calorie‑dense, so they should be consumed in moderate portions.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: They contain oxalates, which can be an issue for individuals prone to kidney stones.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pine nuts can be enjoyed as a snack, tossed into salads, blended into sauces, added to rice, couscous, baked goods, or made into pesto. Light toasting enhances their aroma. Soaking raw nuts for 2–4 hours can improve digestibility.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store pine nuts in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation. Discard nuts that develop a rancid smell.
